items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: I worked out of New York with the group I told you about -- the trio with Sir Charles and Luis Gonsales.

ctx.x: You were in New York, though. You mentioned something about being there in '44, didn't you.

Yeah, I was there in '44, but I was working out of New York more than... Well, my family lived in Brooklyn, I stayed with them, and I worked out of New York with the group I told you about -- the trio with Sir Charles and Luis Gonsales. Also we used to sing a lot of things. Because I used to write a lot of little songs. Like "Baby, I'm Gone" and stuff like that we used to sing. And we made records of those things. I used to record for Exclusive Records, which was a Leon René company. Herb Jeffries also recorded…

items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Tell me about your association with Charlie Mingus. You taught him, right?

ctx.x: Was this after he'd left Los Angeles, or while he was still living here?

Oh, this was after he'd left Los Angeles and had become a big name even! You know, he trusted us. He knew that if he was anywhere near us, everything would be all right. As a matter of fact, I was in Honolulu, and he had gone with Lionel Hampton -- this was something I didn't know anything about it. I don't know how he tracked me down, but he did. I had a girlfriend who used to run a record shop, and the phone rings, and it's a call from somewhere, and it's Charlie Mingus. He'd tracked me down, and he had just…
How long did he study with you?

items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: I couldn't bring myself to put my own name down on Callender's bass, so I put Red Calloway's name down.

ctx.x: No, I didn't get my money. "Mingus (See Insert, p.31) I forgot most of that. There's a bridge to everything on that. Fingers, (inaudible). ^ (Singing.) ^ That's so long ago, I sung it out of tune. Plus, I've forgotten the bridge. (Singing.)

I got DownBeat in there some kind of way. In those days, That's something else about cheating, man; those polls they used to have, Lionel always, (inaudible). ^ A truck backed up to a theater stage where we were playing. We had a week in the theater, and a truck backed up and dumped off some DownBeat magazines. Except n't said they were magazines. They were tearsheets from the poll. Also, I blew for a half-hour. He got everybody voted for Hamp. to do it. But that year Red Callender got a whole lot of votes…
But Benny Goodman was there then, too, so he bought more DownBeats than anybody, so he won.
